qualifying_findings.source_title: Dockerless Verification Is The Next Coding Agent Bottleneck
qualifying_findings.summary: Developers Digest analyzed ByteDance's Dockerless verifier paper and framed environment-free patch checking as a cheaper evidence layer before spending CI, reviewer, or sandbox time on coding-agent patches.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Verification guidance should distinguish pre-CI evidence gathering from authoritative CI and should capture when repository exploration, static checks, and verifier scores are triage signals rather than final acceptance.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route paper and benchmark background upstream if needed; keep local practice implications for verification-loop design and acceptance-gate economics.

qualifying_findings.source_title: AI Dev News: Week of July 12, 2026
qualifying_findings.summary: Developers Digest highlighted a coordinated agent rewrite of a JavaScript runtime with adversarial code review and also flagged a prompt-injection incident involving GitHub agents in the same weekly AI development roundup.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Multi-agent implementation claims should be captured as workflow evidence only when paired with review topology, regression proof, and adversarial review details; prompt-injection mentions reinforce the need for untrusted-issue and repository-content boundaries.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Broad product, model, and runtime news belongs upstream; retain local notes about adversarial review topology and prompt-injection gates.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Are Podcasts the New Playbook for Engineering Leaders Work through AI in the SDLC?
qualifying_findings.summary: Futurum framed Qodo's engineering podcast guide as a signal that engineering leaders need practical AI literacy for evaluating, deploying, and governing AI-assisted development tools as agentic deployments move toward production.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Adoption guidance should include leader-facing literacy, evaluation, and governance decision support, not only developer tool onboarding; the source also reinforces reliability and hallucination management as production-rollout concerns.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep company and media-property background upstream; retain downstream operating-model implications for leader enablement and governance literacy.

qualifying_findings.source_title: What Is an LLM Gateway? A Complete Guide
qualifying_findings.summary: TrueFoundry described an LLM gateway as a middleware/control layer that routes requests across providers, enforces authentication and rate limits, tracks cost, applies governance, and handles failover through one API.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Local tool-governance and harness pages should treat gateways as operational control planes for policy, observability, cost, and failover rather than only provider abstraction or model routing.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Product/vendor comparison belongs upstream; keep local practice implications for centralized governance, observability, cost tracking, and failover.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Forget typosquatting; slopsquatting is the software supply chain threat created by AI coding tools
qualifying_findings.summary: VentureBeat reported on slopsquatting as a supply-chain threat in which attackers exploit AI coding assistants' hallucinated package names by registering plausible malicious dependencies.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: AI-assisted coding controls should validate newly introduced dependencies against registries, provenance, allowlists, lockfiles, and human review instead of trusting generated package names or scaffolded install commands.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep broad security technique background upstream; retain local practice implications for package-install risk, dependency gates, and generated-code review.
